problems.stem: A CAT 100 assignment says: "You may use AI to brainstorm, but the final draft must be your own words and you must disclose any AI use." You used AI to brainstorm three topic ideas, then wrote the essay yourself. What is the correct disclosure?
options: Write nothing, since the final words are yours.
Add a note: "Used ChatGPT on 6/3 to brainstorm three topic ideas; selected one and wrote the draft myself."
Add "AI-assisted" with no detail about what AI did.
Claim no AI use because brainstorming does not count.
problems.explanation: The policy allows brainstorming but requires disclosure. A specific note of what AI did, and when, meets the rule even though the words are your own.

problems.stem: Your ENGL course let you use AI to outline essays. Your CAT 100 assignment's syllabus says "no AI for graded writing." You want to use AI to outline the CAT 100 essay. What is the defensible move?
options: Use AI to outline; the ENGL rule shows it is generally acceptable.
Follow the CAT 100 syllabus: do not use AI for this graded writing, and ask the instructor if any AI step is unclear.
Use AI but do not mention it, since rules differ between courses anyway.
Ask a classmate from ENGL whether the CAT 100 rule really applies.
problems.explanation: AI rules are set per assignment and syllabus. A rule from one course does not transfer; follow this course's stated policy and ask when unclear.

problems.stem: An assignment permits AI "for spelling and grammar only." You paste your finished paragraph and the AI both fixes commas and rewrites your thesis into a stronger argument. What should you submit?
options: The full AI version, including the rewritten thesis, since it is better.
Keep only the grammar and comma fixes; restore your own thesis, because rewriting the argument exceeds the permitted use.
Submit the AI thesis but credit it in a footnote.
Reject all changes, including the grammar fixes that were allowed.
problems.explanation: Proofreading was allowed; generating a new thesis was not. Accept the permitted edits and reject the part that crosses the boundary.

problems.stem: You hand-reword every sentence an AI generated so the wording is entirely yours. The assignment requires disclosure of AI use. Do you still disclose?
options: No, because none of the original AI words remain.
Yes, because the AI shaped the ideas and the draft, which is what disclosure covers.
Only if more than half the words are still the AI's.
Only if the instructor specifically asks you later.
problems.explanation: Disclosure tracks the source of the ideas and drafting help, not surface wording. Rewording does not erase the AI's contribution to the content.
